summary:
In September 1943, German troops massacred Italian prisoners of war from the Acqui Division on Cephalonia after the Italians resisted disarmament following Italy’s armistice with the Allies. The fighting began on 13 September; the last Italian forces surrendered on 22 September after running out of ammunition. About 1,315 Italians were killed in battle.

German troops then executed 5,155 prisoners by 26 September, including General Antonio Gandin and many officers. Around 3,000 more Italian prisoners drowned when ships carrying them to German camps were sunk by Allied attacks or mines. The killings were carried out mainly by troops of the German 1st Mountain Division.

General Hubert Lanz, the division’s senior commander, was sentenced to 12 years in prison for the massacre and other atrocities in Greece; he was released in 1951. Major Harald von Hirschfeld, who led German forces on Cephalonia, died in combat before the end of the war and was never tried.
